seoTitle: How to Find Your TradingView ID Easily
metaDescription: Learn where to find your TradingView user ID and username for scripts, alerts, broker connections, or support requests, and how to copy your profile link.
intro: Whether you need your TradingView ID for a support ticket, a broker connection, or sharing your profile, it's easy to confuse it with your username or profile link — TradingView doesn't display a separate numeric ID anywhere obvious, and what most tools actually mean by "ID" is your username. This guide shows exactly where to find it: the account menu, your public profile page, and, for anyone who needs the literal string as it's stored in the page itself, a quick way to confirm it using the browser's built-in inspector.

steps.heading: Open TradingView and find your account icon
steps.body: Log in at tradingview.com and look at the top-right corner of any page — your account avatar sits there as a small colored circle with your initial, next to the Upgrade button. This icon is your entry point for everything account-related, including the username that functions as your TradingView ID. It's the same spot whether you're looking at a chart, the markets homepage, or a symbol page, so it's worth remembering as the one consistent place to start.

image.caption: The TradingView homepage with the account avatar visible in the top-right corner, next to the Upgrade button.

steps.heading: Open the account menu
steps.body: Click your avatar icon to open the account dropdown. This menu shows your display name at the top — in this example, "PMN_Online1" — along with links to Settings and billing, Refer a friend, Help Center, and Sign Out, plus toggles for dark theme and language. The name shown here at the top of the menu is your TradingView username, and for the vast majority of purposes — support tickets, broker connection forms, sharing your account with someone else — this is the "ID" people are actually asking for.

image.caption: The account dropdown opened from the avatar icon, showing the username at the top above Settings and billing.

steps.heading: Visit your public profile page
steps.body: Click your username in the dropdown, or navigate to tradingview.com/u/yourusername/, to land on your public profile. The username appears again here as a large heading above your Followers, Following, Ideas, and Scripts counts, along with your join date. This profile URL is what you copy and share when someone asks for your TradingView link — for scripts you've published, for a broker asking to verify your account, or for support staff who need to look up your account by name rather than email.

steps.heading: Confirm the exact ID string if a script or integration needs it
steps.body: Some scripts, indicator integrations, and broker connection forms ask for your ID as an exact string, and it's worth double-checking there's no hidden formatting difference from what's displayed. Right-click your username on the profile page and choose Inspect to open the browser's developer tools; the element panel shows the username sitting inside an h1 heading tag exactly as text, with no extra numeric ID appended anywhere nearby. Seeing it in the raw HTML like this confirms that what's displayed on the page is the whole string — there's no separate hidden identifier you're missing.

image.caption: The profile page with developer tools open, showing the username sitting as plain text inside the page's heading element.

steps.heading: Copy and share it correctly
steps.body: When a form or support agent asks for your TradingView ID, the safest answer is your full profile URL rather than just the bare username, since it removes any ambiguity about capitalization or which platform you mean. Triple-click the username on your profile page to select it cleanly, or copy the URL directly from your browser's address bar while on your profile. Avoid typing it from memory for anything account-critical like a broker link — a single mistyped character sends the wrong account into someone else's system.

faq.question: Is my TradingView ID the same as my username?
faq.answer: Yes. TradingView doesn't issue a separate numeric account ID for everyday use — the username shown in your account menu and on your profile page is what support requests, broker integrations, and script sharing all refer to as your ID.

faq.question: Why do I need my TradingView ID?
faq.answer: It's commonly needed for support requests, connecting broker integrations, or sharing scripts and profiles with other users. Providing your full profile link instead of just the username avoids any confusion.

faq.question: Can I change my TradingView username/ID?
faq.answer: TradingView allows username changes from Settings and billing in the account menu, though there may be limits on how often you can change it, and your old profile link will stop working once you do.

faq.question: Where do I find my ID on mobile?
faq.answer: Open your profile from the account menu in the TradingView mobile app — your username is displayed the same way as on desktop, at the top of your profile page.

faq.question: Is there a hidden numeric ID behind my TradingView username?
faq.answer: Checking the page's underlying HTML shows the username as the only identifying text tied to your profile heading — there's no separate numeric ID displayed or needed for standard use like scripts, alerts, or support tickets.
